post.description:
Requires prior JWT authentication — gated here via
`Depends(require_any())` (zero-arg: "just authenticated", row 25's
catch-all), matching Group 4's resolution that this endpoint is *not*
in the permitAll matrix despite not being under `/api/`. Because that
dependency already 401s (generic legacy envelope, not the OAuth2 shape)
before this handler body ever runs, `validate_authorize_request`'s step
7 ("User must be authenticated" -> `unauthorized_client`) can never
actually fire through this route — `principal` is guaranteed non-`None`
here. It's preserved in the pure validation function anyway for
fidelity to spec.md's 7-step order and so it stays directly testable;
this mirrors the project's existing pattern of documenting
preserved-but-unreachable code paths (e.g. Group 10's
`FactorVersionOverlapException`, Group 4's row-10 matrix note).

Dispatches on `grant_type` to one of the 3 supported grants. An
unrecognized/missing `grant_type` is not explicitly specified by
spec.md (which only documents the 3 known grants' internal behavior) —
`unsupported_grant_type` is the natural fit among the existing
`OAuth2Error` codes and is used here as a reasonable default.

RFC 7662. Requires OAuth2 client authentication (same dual Basic/
body-credential path as the token-exchange grant). A missing or
unparseable `token` is **not** an error — it's a valid `200
{"active": false}` response per RFC 7662.

AcceptedSwapProposalResponse.title: AcceptedSwapProposalResponse
AcceptedSwapProposalResponse.description:
Accept response: the proposal plus where and when the swap happens.
For an event swap `term_id`/`group_id` are null, `term_occurs_on` is the
event start and `group_name` the event name; a personal swap has all four

BrowseTermItemListingResponse.title: BrowseTermItemListingResponse
BrowseTermItemListingResponse.description:
One row of "Twoje wystawione rzeczy" (`list_my_term_item_listings`)
or "Rzeczy od innych" (`list_browsable_term_item_listings`) — one
`ItemListingPreference`, resolved against `term_id`, plus the cross-BC
display data (product name/condition from `app.circulation`/
`app.product`, lister display name from `app.users`) and derived
status (`resolved_reservation_id`/`taken_by_party_id`, from the item's
own live `Reservation` history — see `_resolve_listing_status`; a
pending swap proposer's reservation or party is never exposed). `id` is
the item's id: one derived listing per item, not per creation event.

CancelTransactionResponse.description:
Same `status`/`already_resolved` discriminator pattern as
`ConfirmTransactionResponse` — see that model's docstring.

CategoryResponse.title: CategoryResponse
CategoryResponse.description:
`product_count` is an aggregated value, never a plain ORM attribute
on `Category` — so `category_response_from` below is the construction
entry point routers/service use instead of a plain
`model_validate(from_attributes)` call, mirroring `app/plugin/
schemas.py`'s `plugin_response_from_descriptor`.

`inventory_type` and `owner_user_id` are `None` for the EXTERNAL
account.

ClientRegistrationRequest.title: ClientRegistrationRequest
ClientRegistrationRequest.description:
All fields optional at the wire level — validation (with spec.md's
exact messages) happens explicitly in the handler, not via Pydantic's
own 422 machinery, since the required/default/conditional rules don't
map onto plain field constraints.

ConfirmTransactionResponse.title: ConfirmTransactionResponse
ConfirmTransactionResponse.description:
`already_resolved` is the explicit discriminator the frontend uses
to render "too late, the other party already resolved this" distinctly
from a generic error, per spec.md Requirement 3. It is only ever `True`
when this response accompanies a 409 (the reservation itself carries no
"already resolved" status of its own — see `TermAlreadyResolvedException`).

ConversationResponse.title: ConversationResponse
ConversationResponse.description:
`participant_count` counts account-backed parties (GROUP, TERM and
EVENT).

CreateCategoryRequest.title: CreateCategoryRequest
CreateCategoryRequest.description:
`parent_id` null creates a root; there is no reparenting later.
Names are stripped, so a blank name fails `min_length` and a padded one
meets the sibling uniqueness check.

CreateFamilyRequest.title: CreateFamilyRequest
CreateFamilyRequest.description:
Bootstraps a Family group and its first guardian in one call —
creates a brand new login (`auth.User`) for the guardian, since there is
no other identity primitive available.

CreateInventoryItemRequest.title: CreateInventoryItemRequest
CreateInventoryItemRequest.description:
`listing_mode` `None` registers a draft; GIFT/SWAP offers the item
right away (PERSONAL inventory only, in the same commit). `location_id`
is one of the caller's own live saved places.

CreateLightweightMemberRequest.title: CreateLightweightMemberRequest
CreateLightweightMemberRequest.description:
One entry of a `POST /api/families/mine/members` batch — a family
member with no login of their own (see
`app.families.service.create_lightweight_family_member`).

CreateOwnCircleRequest.title: CreateOwnCircleRequest
CreateOwnCircleRequest.description:
`visibility` and the defaults are honoured by `/mine/new` only;
`/mine` ignores them.

CreateOwnFamilyRequest.title: CreateOwnFamilyRequest
CreateOwnFamilyRequest.description:
Self-service "create my family" with a caller-supplied name — the
caller's party id always comes from the principal, never the body.

CreateTermRequest.title: CreateTermRequest
CreateTermRequest.description:
`location_id`/`capacity` omitted -> copied from the Circle's defaults
(told apart via `model_fields_set`); a term without any place is rejected.

EventDetailResponse.title: EventDetailResponse
EventDetailResponse.description:
The event page: the public event plus what the page needs around it.
`participants` lists the author first, then active attendees in sign-up
order; `attendee_count` excludes the author. `open_reservations` is
filled for the author only.

EventOpenReservationsResponse.title: EventOpenReservationsResponse
EventOpenReservationsResponse.description:
What deleting the event would cancel: open gift reservations plus
open swaps (`total`), of which `swaps` are swaps.

EventOrganizationResponse.title: EventOrganizationResponse
EventOrganizationResponse.description: The author's own Organization: its name and stored theme colors.

EventParticipantItemResponse.title: EventParticipantItemResponse
EventParticipantItemResponse.description:
`added_at` is the listing preference's `created_at` (naive UTC);
`reservation` is `None` while the item is available.

EventParticipantResponse.title: EventParticipantResponse
EventParticipantResponse.description:
`items` holds at most the 3 newest listed items; `items_total` counts
them all.

FamilyExchangeDetailResponse.title: FamilyExchangeDetailResponse
FamilyExchangeDetailResponse.description:
`GET /api/groups/{id}/families/{family_id}/exchange-offers` body —
every active offer from any guardian of the requested family.

FamilyExchangeOffer.title: FamilyExchangeOffer
FamilyExchangeOffer.description:
One active exchange-mechanism offer from any guardian of a given
family, for the family card's "DO WYMIANY W GRUPIE" section — field
shape reused 1:1 from `BrowseTermItemListingResponse` (`product_name`,
`condition`, `offered_types`), per spec.md's reuse note.

FamilyExchangeSummary.title: FamilyExchangeSummary
FamilyExchangeSummary.description:
One family's "udostępnia rzecz"/"przynosi na zajęcia" status marks
for the group's current Term, in `get_group_exchange_summary`'s
stable, family-order-preserving output — see
`app/groups/application/exchange_summary.py`.

GroupAccessDetails.title: GroupAccessDetails
GroupAccessDetails.description:
The caller's relationship to a Circle, resolved server-side so the
frontend never has to infer "can I see this / do I need a code" from
raw auth-token presence — the previous `token ? private-view :
public-view` frontend branching treated ANY logged-in principal as if
they belonged to every Circle, which is wrong (see `GroupAccessResponse`).

GroupAccessResponse.title: GroupAccessResponse
GroupAccessResponse.description:
`GET /api/public/groups/{group_id}/access` — the Circle's public
identity plus the caller's resolved access, in one call. `group` reuses
`PublicCircleResponse`'s already-privacy-safe shape (a `PRIVATE` group's
response still omits `term`/`guardians` regardless of `access`).

GroupExchangeSummaryResponse.title: GroupExchangeSummaryResponse
GroupExchangeSummaryResponse.description:
`GET /api/groups/{id}/exchange-summary` body — one
`FamilyExchangeSummary` per family currently in the group.

GroupLayoutMode.title: GroupLayoutMode
GroupLayoutMode.description:
The participant-visualization layout an organizer picks for their
Circle's `/krag/{id}` screen — `CIRCLE` is the long-standing layout,
`PITCH`/`TABLE` are the two new algorithmic layouts. A stable, always-
sensible default (`CIRCLE`), so the column carries a permanent
`server_default` rather than a temporary backfill one — see the
`0035_group_layout_mode` migration's docstring.

GroupMemberResponse.title: GroupMemberResponse
GroupMemberResponse.description:
One party who RSVP'd (and did not withdraw) to at least one Term of
a Group, resolved for the group details page — `terms_attended` is how
many of the group's Terms they signed up for, `last_term_on` the most
recent of those (Warsaw wall-clock, like `TermResponse.occurs_on`).
`family_name` is display-only, `None` for a family-less party.

GroupVisibility.title: GroupVisibility
GroupVisibility.description:
`PUBLIC` (default): anyone with the link may RSVP to a Term.
`PRIVATE`: only existing standing `Membership` members (or the active
organizer) may RSVP or see the Circle's content; an outsider joins with
the organizer's access code (`Group.join_code`), whose redemption creates
the `Membership` — never anonymous per-term RSVP. Visibility changes only
via `PATCH /groups/{id}` (`update_group`); it is fully independent of
standing-`Membership` creation.

GuardianResponse.title: GuardianResponse
GuardianResponse.description:
Denormalized join of `FamilyMembership` + `UserProfile` — the
caller shouldn't need a second round trip to find out who a guardian
is or whether they're the family's primary contact.

ItemActionsResponse.title: ItemActionsResponse
ItemActionsResponse.description:
The item page's action read model. `mode` is null without a listing
preference; `available` means listed (ACTIVE), AVAILABLE and without a
pending swap proposal; `reservation` is the reserved badge (null while
nobody reserves the item); `visibility` is the listing's visibility for
its owner and null for anyone else or without a listing preference;
`contexts` holds at most 5 upcoming contexts the viewer may see.

ItemContextOptionResponse.title: ItemContextOptionResponse
ItemContextOptionResponse.description:
An upcoming term or event the owner takes part in. `eligible` is
whether the logged-in, non-owner viewer may reserve in it.

ItemContextResponse.title: ItemContextResponse
ItemContextResponse.description:
The term or event an item is reserved in. `name` is the circle's name
for a term; `starts_at` is naive Warsaw wall clock.

ItemDetailsResponse.title: ItemDetailsResponse
ItemDetailsResponse.description:
`GET /api/public/items/{id}/details` — the item page's read
model. Carries no user, inventory or reservation ids.

ItemHistoryEntryResponse.title: ItemHistoryEntryResponse
ItemHistoryEntryResponse.description:

history`. Deliberately no ids and no raw transaction description.

ItemListingStatus.title: ItemListingStatus

ItemPartyReservationResponse.title: ItemPartyReservationResponse
ItemPartyReservationResponse.description:

ItemTakeRequest.description: Only `GIFT` is taken directly; a SWAP goes through the propose route.

ItemTakeResponse.title: ItemTakeResponse

owner's listings. `PRIVATE`: only people in the owner's private groups.
Stored on `ItemListingPreference`, so an unlisted item has none.

JoinCodeResponse.title: JoinCodeResponse
JoinCodeResponse.description: The only schema that carries a Circle's join code — organizer-only.

LeadershipResponse.title: LeadershipResponse

`service.py`, not stored on the row) so callers don't need a second

LocalitySearchResponse.description: `total` counts every match, not only the returned `results`.

LocalitySearchResult.title: LocalitySearchResult

LocationRequest.title: LocationRequest

as null. `source` is required with an address and forbidden without
one; GOOGLE requires `google_place_id`, `lat` and `lng`, MANUAL forbids
them. The owner is always the caller, never a body field.

LocationResponse.title: LocationResponse

declared `float` here so JSON carries numbers, not strings.

MembershipResponse.title: MembershipResponse

`has_more` means older messages exist; with `after`, newer ones do.

ModerationQueueEntryResponse.title: ModerationQueueEntryResponse
ModerationQueueEntryResponse.description:
One photo awaiting (or past) a decision. `scores` are the latest
model scores, `null` when no model has scored it.

ModerationTermResponse.title: ModerationTermResponse
ModerationTermResponse.description:
`GET /api/terms/moderation` (ADMIN-only) row: a Term of any Circle
with the Circle's name and its active (non-withdrawn) signup counts.

MovementType.title: MovementType
MovementType.description:
GIFT/SWAP share their values with `ReservationType`, so a fulfilled
reservation maps to `MovementType(reservation_type.value)`. LEND/RETURN
are no longer posted but stay loadable for existing item history.

MyAttendanceResponse.title: MyAttendanceResponse
MyAttendanceResponse.description:
One row of the caller's own Term RSVPs — carries enough to render a
panel tile (date, circle name, organizer) and rebuild the public-term
link (`organizer_slug` + `group_id` + `term_id`) with no second request.
`organizer_display_name` is `None` when the circle currently has no
active organizer; `organizer_slug` is always usable (falls back to a
stable hash — see `service.resolve_organizer_slug`).

MyInventoryItemResponse.title: MyInventoryItemResponse
MyInventoryItemResponse.description:
One row of `GET /api/inventory-items/mine` — an item physically in
the caller's PERSONAL inventory together with its
standing `ItemListingPreference.mode` and `visibility` (both `None` =
not offered), so
`Moje rzeczy` only ever shows and seeds toggles for items at home.
`photos_moderation_pending` is true while the item's product has a
PENDING/NEEDS_REVIEW photo; it is informational only and does not
block listing the item.
`thumb_url` is the product's first APPROVED photo (400 px), `None`
without one or without object storage. `location_id` is the item's
place as stored, soft-deleted or not.

MyPledgeResponse.title: MyPledgeResponse
MyPledgeResponse.description:
One row of the caller's own "rzeczy, które obiecałem przynieść" list —
carries enough to render a panel tile and rebuild the public-term link
(`organizer_slug` + `group_id` + `term_id`).

MyReservationResponse.title: MyReservationResponse
MyReservationResponse.description:
One row of `GET /api/reservations/mine`: an item the caller is about
to receive. `PROPOSED` is the caller's swap offer still awaiting the
owner (`reservation_id` `None`); `PENDING`/`CONFIRMED` is their open
reservation.

MyTermResponse.title: MyTermResponse
MyTermResponse.description:
`GET /api/groups/mine/terms` row: only what a `/meetings` card shows —
the Term with its circle's name and public-URL slug, so the panel needs no
per-circle read. `attendee_count`/`child_count` are set for led terms.

MyTermRole.title: MyTermRole
MyTermRole.description:
`led`: circles the caller leads; `member`: PRIVATE circles the caller
or their family belongs to, without the led ones.

NotificationKind.title: NotificationKind
NotificationKind.description:
What happened. The recipient differs by kind: the first two go to a
Term's organizer, `NEEDED_ITEM_REMOVED` goes to the affected pledger,
`TERM_ITEM_LISTING_TAKEN` goes to the lister whose offered item was just
taken by another attendee, `ITEM_RESERVED_FOR_PICKUP` goes to the taker
of a term listing at take time, `SWAP_PROPOSED` goes to the target listing's
owner, `SWAP_ACCEPTED`/`SWAP_REJECTED` go back to the swap's proposer,
`TERM_CONFIRMATION_NEEDED` goes to both parties of an `ACCEPTED` swap
or of a still-open GIFT reservation once its Term ends, and
`TERM_ALREADY_RESOLVED` goes to the other party in a swap/giveaway when
they act after the first party already resolved the same transaction,
and `RESERVATION_CANCELLED` goes to both parties of a reservation or
swap cancelled because its event was deleted.

OrganizationGroupTermsResponse.title: OrganizationGroupTermsResponse
OrganizationGroupTermsResponse.description:
The group page behind `/<org-slug>/group/<group-id>/terms`: the group
tile and its upcoming terms, earliest first, at most
`GROUP_TERMS_LIMIT`.

OwnerMediaResponse.title: OwnerMediaResponse
OwnerMediaResponse.description: APPROVED rows carry public CDN URLs, the rest presigned ones.

OwnerMeetingsResponse.title: OwnerMeetingsResponse
OwnerMeetingsResponse.description:
The owner meetings page (`/<org-slug>/meetings`, `/<party-id>/meetings`):
the owner's upcoming public terms and events, earliest first, at most
`OWNER_MEETINGS_LIMIT`.

PartyProfileResponse.title: PartyProfileResponse
PartyProfileResponse.description:
The public profile of a person (`/<party-id>`): always the person
(`owner` with their own name and no slug); an Organization they own is a
separate page, linked through `organization`.

PluginResponse.title: PluginResponse
PluginResponse.description:
Field order mirrors the Java DTO: `id, name, version, url,
description, enabled, extension_points`.

ProductPhotoResponse.title: ProductPhotoResponse
ProductPhotoResponse.description:
`url` is the 1600 px WebP, `thumb_url` the 400 px one. Non-approved
photos (shown to item owners only) carry short-lived signed URLs.

ProductResponse.title: ProductResponse
ProductResponse.description:
Field order is significant (mirrors the Java DTO): `id, name,
description, photo_url, sku, category_id, plugin_data, created_at,
updated_at`.

PublicCircleOrganization.title: PublicCircleOrganization
PublicCircleOrganization.description:
The organizer's own Organization: its name and stored colors, reported
as-is; the frontend decides how (and whether) to derive a palette from
them. `palette_preset` is the stored preset key, or `None`.

PublicCircleResponse.title: PublicCircleResponse
PublicCircleResponse.description:
Never carries a per-child field — `guardians` exposes only the
aggregate `child_count` each guardian RSVP'd with (see
`TermAttendance`), so there is nothing per-attendee to leak.

PublicItemListingResponse.title: PublicItemListingResponse
PublicItemListingResponse.description:
One exchange-mechanism offer for the public Term page, available or
reserved (see `list_public_term_item_listings`). `id` is the item's id,
same convention as `BrowseTermItemListingResponse`.

PublicLocationResponse.title: PublicLocationResponse
PublicLocationResponse.description: The place as others see it: never the owner's party id, no timestamps.

PublicOrganizationResponse.title: PublicOrganizationResponse
PublicOrganizationResponse.description:
Served from the unauthenticated `/api/public/organizations/{slug}`
endpoint — deliberately a narrower shape than `OrganizationResponse`:
no `party_id`/timestamps, nothing beyond what the public page itself
displays. `page_layout` is the effective layout (`resolve_page_layout`),
unlike the owner's `OrganizationResponse`, which carries the stored key.
The media fields default to empty; the API router fills them.

RedeemJoinCodeResponse.title: RedeemJoinCodeResponse
RedeemJoinCodeResponse.description:
`created` is false when the caller already had access (organizer or
active member) — nothing was inserted.

RegisterRequest.title: RegisterRequest
RegisterRequest.description:
Public self-registration: bootstraps a login + `Party(PERSON)` +
`UserProfile` only. `username`/`display_name` are derived server-side
from `email` (never accepted from the client — see `service.py`'s
`derive_username_from_email`/`_derive_display_name`); no `Family`/`Circle` is
created here (see spec.md Core Requirement 3).

ReservationContextRef.title: ReservationContextRef
ReservationContextRef.description:
Where a take/propose happens: a term or event by id, or a personal
pickup at the owner's place, which carries no id.

ReservationDetailResponse.title: ReservationDetailResponse
ReservationDetailResponse.description:
`GET /api/reservations/{id}` — adds the context date (the Term's
`occurs_on` or the Event's `starts_at`), read through the keep-live
`find_reservation_context_occurs_on` so it still resolves once the
Term's group is soft-deleted (`GET /api/terms/{id}` then answers 404).
`personal_pickup` marks an open reservation with neither context.

ReservationType.title: ReservationType
ReservationType.description:
Only `SWAP`/`GIFT` reservations are created; `LEND`/`RETURN` stay
loadable for existing rows.

ResolveProductRequest.title: ResolveProductRequest
ResolveProductRequest.description:
`POST /api/products/resolve` — resolves a freeform item name (e.g.
typed during onboarding) to an existing `Product`, or creates one on the
fly with a placeholder sku. Reuses `ProductResponse` as the return
shape; no dedicated response schema.

SendMessageRequest.title: SendMessageRequest
SendMessageRequest.description:
The 1–1000 character rule is checked on the trimmed body in
`application/messages.py` so it answers with Polish copy.

SetItemListingPreferenceRequest.title: SetItemListingPreferenceRequest
SetItemListingPreferenceRequest.description:
`mode=None` clears the item's standing listing preference. An omitted
`visibility` keeps the current one (PUBLIC for a new row); it is refused
without a mode, so a visibility change can never clear the listing.

SwapProposalOfferResponse.title: SwapProposalOfferResponse
SwapProposalOfferResponse.description:
One pending offer against one of the caller's own SWAP-listed items
(`GET /api/term-item-listings/{item_id}/swap-proposals`) — enough to
render "X oferuje Y" and let the owner `acceptSwapProposal` directly,
without a second round trip to resolve the proposer's name or their
offered item's product.

TermAttendeeChildResponse.title: TermAttendeeChildResponse
TermAttendeeChildResponse.description:
An active CHILD member of an attendee's family, age only — no name
or id is exposed to the organizer.

TermAttendeeResponse.title: TermAttendeeResponse
TermAttendeeResponse.description:
One RSVP'd party for a chosen Term, resolved for the organizer's
attendee list. `family_id`/`family_name` are display-only — `None` for a
family-less attendee (e.g. an anonymous guest party). `children` is
youngest first, unknown years last.

TermPeriod.title: TermPeriod
TermPeriod.description:
`upcoming`: from the start of today (Warsaw) on, earliest first;
`past`: before it, latest first.

UpdateEventRequest.title: UpdateEventRequest
UpdateEventRequest.description:
Only the fields present in the body change; each one is checked by
the same rules as on create.

UpdateFamilyMemberRequest.title: UpdateFamilyMemberRequest
UpdateFamilyMemberRequest.description:
Birth-year-only edit of a CHILD member. The key is required (an
explicit `null` clears the year) and nothing else may be sent.

UpdateFamilyRequest.title: UpdateFamilyRequest
UpdateFamilyRequest.description:
Guardian-only in-place rename — the guardian check lives in
`service.rename_family`, not the matrix.

UpdateGroupRequest.title: UpdateGroupRequest
UpdateGroupRequest.description:
In-place circle update — the active-organizer check lives in
`service.update_group`, not the matrix. `name` is required;
`layout_mode`/`visibility` apply only when non-null; the defaults apply
only when present in `model_fields_set` (omitted = keep, `null` = clear).

UpdateInventoryItemRequest.title: UpdateInventoryItemRequest
UpdateInventoryItemRequest.description:
PATCH `/api/inventory-items/{id}` body. All fields optional and
partial-apply. `product_id` re-points the item at a different entry in
the shared `Product` catalog — the frontend resolves a Product by
name+category first, then sends its id here to rename/re-categorise.
`location_id` moves the item to another own live place; an item can
never lose its place by PATCH, so an explicit `null` is rejected.

UpdateMyProfileAppearanceRequest.title: UpdateMyProfileAppearanceRequest
UpdateMyProfileAppearanceRequest.description:
A `PATCH` of the caller's public profile appearance ("Wygląd strony"):
an omitted field stays unchanged, an explicit `null` clears
`palette_preset` / `primary_color` / `accent_color` / `bio` (a blank `bio`
clears it too). `page_layout` cannot be cleared, so `null` is rejected
(400). Unknown keys are rejected too. The service applies exactly the
fields present in `model_fields_set`.

UpdateMyProfileRequest.title: UpdateMyProfileRequest
UpdateMyProfileRequest.description: The caller's own editable profile fields. A blank `bio` clears it.

UpdateOrganizationRequest.title: UpdateOrganizationRequest
UpdateOrganizationRequest.description:
A `PATCH`: an omitted field stays unchanged, an explicit `null`
clears `palette_preset` / `primary_color` / `accent_color` / `description`
(a blank `description` clears it too). `name` and `page_layout` cannot be
cleared, so `null` for them is rejected (400).
Unknown keys are rejected too. The service applies exactly the fields
present in `model_fields_set`.

UpdateTermRequest.title: UpdateTermRequest
UpdateTermRequest.description:
`occurs_on`/`description` apply only when non-null; `location_id`/
`capacity` apply when present in `model_fields_set` (`null` clears the
capacity; a `null` place is rejected).

WithdrawAttendanceResponse.title: WithdrawAttendanceResponse
WithdrawAttendanceResponse.description:
Bare `TermAttendance` row returned by
`POST /api/groups/mine/attendances/{id}/withdraw` — `withdrawn_at`
is the field callers check to confirm the (idempotent) withdrawal.

app__events__schemas__ReservedByResponse.title: ReservedByResponse
app__events__schemas__ReservedByResponse.description:
The groups reserved badge: `by_name` (the party who would receive the
item, `None` for an anonymous viewer) and whether that is the viewer.

app__groups__schemas__ReservedByResponse.title: ReservedByResponse
app__groups__schemas__ReservedByResponse.description:
A listed item's reserved badge. `by_name` is the party who would
receive the item (the taker or swap counterparty, or the proposer of a
pending swap proposal), `None` for an anonymous viewer; `by_me` is true
when the viewer is that party.
